title: Seller demands advance to personal UPI vs. seller ships cash on delivery
summary: The recipient is a buyer who marked interest in a used camera listed on BechoBazaar by a seller in another city. The seller messages back, confirms the item, and offers to ship it through SwiftShip Couriers. In the legitimate case, the seller books the parcel as cash on delivery so the buyer pays the courier on arrival after checking the item. In the fraud case, the seller demands the full price to a personal UPI ID before shipping and refuses any pay-on-delivery option. Both sellers mention UPI, shipping, and payment; the difference is who bears the risk and when money moves.

fraud.label_rationale: The seller requires full payment to a personal UPI ID before dispatch and refuses cash on delivery, so the buyer carries all the risk for goods they cannot inspect. This is the standard advance-payment pattern of classifieds fraud.
stable_facts: Payment is to [UPI_ID_7], a personal handle with a name different from the listing.
The seller says COD is "not possible because of fake buyers".
The seller promises a SwiftShip tracking number "after payment".

resistant.legitimate: Offers to pay in advance by UPI to speed things up

suspicious.fraud: Says advance to a stranger is risky and asks for COD or a video call
suspicious.legitimate: Asks for a photo of the bill with the seller's name

fraud: seller accepts a "token" advance instead and presses for the rest
buyer refuses and seller stops replying.
legitimate: seller politely declines the offered advance and keeps COD
seller shares a bill photo when asked.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud seller may lower the advance, add urgency ("another buyer is ready"), or send an ID photo. A partial advance is the same mechanism. They must not switch to QR codes for receiving, OTPs, or links. The legitimate seller must not ask for any advance, code, or payment outside the COD parcel.

must_preserve: UPI and shipping wording in both cases
full advance to personal UPI and refusal of COD in _F
COD with payment at the door in _L

ambiguities: A request for advance is not proof of fraud in every real market; in this family the fraud seller also refuses the protected option (COD), which the legitimate seller offers.
Photos, a bill, and polite language appear in both cases and are not cues.
The legitimate seller in _L declines an advance even when offered, so that "advance" words can appear in _L as a confound.

evidence_references.claim: Police advise avoiding advance payments in classifieds deals (CE08)
